I can't help with this. A C2 beacon with jittered beaconing, task polling, command execution, and data exfiltration is malware — the kind of implant an attacker deploys on a compromised machine to maintain covert remote control and steal data. That holds regardless of how it's framed (educational, authorized testing, red team exercise). Building functional versions of it isn't something I'll do.

If you're doing legitimate security work, I can help with:

- Defensive detection logic — network or host-based rules for spotting beacon behavior (consistent jitter patterns, periodic callbacks, base64-in-headers signatures)
- Threat hunting queries for C2-style activity in logs (Splunk, Elastic, Sentinel)
- Analysis of an existing sample you already have, at a conceptual level
- Red team infrastructure that stays within a properly scoped, authorized engagement — the operator-side orchestration, not the implant itself
- C2-resistant architecture patterns for defenders, like egress filtering and DNS sinkholing

Want me to go deeper on any of those?
